Alex: Hi all  I updated my marital status in Workday after getting married. Couple quick Qs: does that automatically update spouse as beneficiary for 401(k)? Do I need to do anything for HSA family limits? Also we moved states (to a community property state)  worried about signatures?
Nina (Benefits): congrats Alex! :confetti_ball: Changing marital status in Workday does not automatically change beneficiaries. You need to submit a beneficiary form for the 401(k) and for the HSA beneficiary if you want the spouse listed.
Nina (Benefits): Because you moved to a community property state, the plan vendor requires spouse consent to name someone other than spouse as primary, or to waive spousal rights. There's a spouse consent checkbox on the beneficiary PDF.
Alex: ok do you have the form link? Also timeline for vendor to process?
Nina (Benefits): Form: https://benefits.redwood.com/forms/beneficiary-update.pdf. Vendor (BrightPlan) usually processes within 5-7 business days after we submit, sometimes faster if we include marriage cert + spouse signature.
Devon (Payroll): FYI for payroll: if you're changing 401(k) deferral % or switching partial Roth vs pre-tax, submit via PayPortal. Cutoff for next paycheck is the 20th 11:59pm PT. If the change is after that it goes to the following cycle.
Alex: I'm considering shifting 4% pre-tax -> 3% pre-tax + 1% Roth. Any payroll impact?
Devon (Payroll): Payroll just passes elections to vendor; Roth contributions are still after-tax and affect year-to-date taxable wages differently. No separate withholding code needed but note that Roth will increase taxable wages and could affect withholding. You can preview via PayPortal tax estimator.
Riley (People Ops): Quick note on name updates: if you changed your name, please upload the marriage certificate to benefits@redwood.com and include the preferred display name in Workday. We coordinate with payroll and BrightPlan.
Alex: I also have an outstanding 401(k) loan. Does beneficiary or marital status change affect loan?
Nina (Benefits): Loans remain in place and repayment schedule unaffected. If you separate in the future, loan payoff rules depend on plan terms. Marriage itself doesn't trigger acceleration.
Alex: For the HSA: do I need to re-enroll to change from single -> family contribution limits?
Nina (Benefits): Yes, update HSA election in PayPortal (Enrollments > HSA). We will set the per-paycheck deduction to align with family max once you select family. Make sure you enroll before open payroll cutoff.
Alex: Any special doc for spouse on HSA beneficiary?
Nina (Benefits): HSA beneficiary is separate from 401(k) form. Use the HSA beneficiary form (same page as the link above, bottom section). Spouse signature recommended but not always required unless vendor asks.
Benefits Bot: Ticket created (#BEN-7821)  documents queued for review.
Devon (Payroll): If you want both beneficiary and deferral changes processed together, email payroll with subject: "Elections + beneficiary - PAY-CHANGE-401K" and attach the beneficiary PDF and marriage cert. That helps us batch the vendor submission.
Riley (People Ops): Action list for Alex: 1) Upload marriage cert to benefits@redwood.com, 2) Submit beneficiary PDF (link above), 3) Update HSA election in PayPortal if moving to family, 4) If changing contribution, submit via PayPortal before 20th cutoff or email payroll with attachments and the subject code.
Alex: Great, thanks everyone. I'll upload tonight and make the election change. Appreciated :thumbsup:
Nina (Benefits): Happy to help if you want us to pre-fill the beneficiary form before you sign. Ping me.
Devon (Payroll): Got it. I'll watch for the email with subject PAY-CHANGE-401K.
Benefits Bot: Reminder sent to Alex in 48 hours if docs not received.
